name: Radius Packaging-West Allis
about:
Radius Packaging, headquartered in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, was founded in 1972. Since its inception, the company has supplied plastic packaging solutions for diverse consumer and industrial markets, building decades-long relationships with brands.

The company operates two facilities, including a 250,000-square-foot plant in Delavan, Wisconsin, that houses both blow molding and injection molding platforms. Radius produces rigid plastic containers from HDPE, PP, and PET, offering capabilities that span custom product development, cellular blow molding for short- to medium-run orders, turn-key injection molding for caps and closures, and value-added services such as high-speed automated labeling, custom packaging, and warehousing programs.

Radius serves the food and specialty beverage, nutrition and wellness, home care, healthcare, and professional cleaning industries. Its customer base includes brands seeking off-the-shelf stock packaging, tailored designs, or fully customized solutions developed from concept through commercialization.

The company emphasizes a holistic approach that integrates manufacturing platforms with design, engineering, and sustainability services. Radius highlights its OSHA SHARP-certified Delavan facility, partnership with the U.S. Army PaYS program, and collaboration with material suppliers like LyondellBasell as differentiators, alongside a track record of industry awards for processing excellence and workplace culture.

name: Railside Furnishings
old_description: Real-Wood Amish Furniture & Dream Kitchens — Built to Last a Lifetime
about:
Railside Furnishings operates from Mifflinburg, Pennsylvania, where it was founded in 2001 as a family-owned venture. The business began with a focus on handcrafted, solid-wood furniture built by Amish craftsmen, a tradition that continues to define its output.

The company produces custom furniture — dining sets, bedroom suites, living room pieces, office furniture, youth collections, and live-edge items — along with fully designed kitchen cabinetry. Each piece is handbuilt by an in-house team or by Amish woodworkers using 100% real wood. The shop also provides 3D renderings for kitchen projects and manages delivery and installation for completed orders.

Railside serves residential customers throughout central Pennsylvania and beyond, selling directly through its showroom and via custom commissions. Homeowners and families make up the core clientele, with projects ranging from single heirloom tables to whole-kitchen renovations.

The founders emphasize a commitment to “German precision and care” rather than luxury branding, citing the use of finest materials and domestic craftsmanship as their guiding principle. The family-owned structure, 25-plus years of design experience, and a promise of prompt communication are presented as the reasons customers return.

Its product lines include Industrial Pie Systems, Readymade Meal Processing, and Industrial Dessert Production, along with OEM-quality replacement chains. Raque differentiates itself by focusing on custom food-packaging machines tailored to each manufacturer’s specific requirements, rejecting a one-size-fits-all approach. The company emphasizes American-built equipment, high-speed production with proven reliability, uncompromising food safety standards, and a service life of three to five years.

name: Ratigan-Schottler Manufacturing
old_description: Ratigan-Schottler Craftsmen have worked in the same workshop, located in Beatrice, Nebraska since 1940.
about:
Ratigan-Schottler Manufacturing has operated from the same workshop in Beatrice, Nebraska since its founding in 1940 by Louie Schottler. The company began as a woodworking shop serving local churches and has remained in the same location for over eight decades, drawing on the region’s tradition of fine craftsmanship.

The firm specializes in solid oak church furniture, producing custom pews, chancel furnishings, liturgical pieces, curved radius pews, and flexible seating. Its 65,000-square-foot facility houses state-of-the-art fabrication equipment where skilled craftsmen handle every step from lumber milling to final assembly. The company reports having served more than 2,500 churches and built over 500,000 linear feet of pews.

Customers are primarily Christian congregations across the United States, including projects in Hawaii. The company’s installation teams travel nationwide to deliver and anchor pews using a concealed anchor system. Past clients include churches in Oklahoma, Minnesota, Illinois, and Wisconsin, as noted in testimonials.

Ratigan-Schottler emphasizes three pillars—craftsmanship, service, and tradition—as its differentiators. It promotes an in-house design team that collaborates directly with clients, a seamless process from quote through follow-up, and a commitment to hand-selected northern hardwoods such as red oak, white oak, maple, mahogany, and cherry.

name: Re-form Office Furniture Reseller & Storage
old_description: Re-form provides delivery and installation services for the mid-Atlantic region. In addition, we have the ability to tap into a national installation network when our clients require out of state deliveries. The Re-form Installation team has been delivering and installing office furniture for years. They have built and installed almost every single make and manufacturer of office furniture. They are skilled craftsman who have a desire to make every installation look beautiful.
about:
Re-form was founded in 1986 in Beltsville, Maryland, after recognizing that businesses struggled to manage increasingly complex office furniture systems and often discarded usable assets. The company began by refurbishing furniture for large corporations and reselling high-quality used systems to smaller organizations across the Mid-Atlantic region, including Aberdeen, Baltimore, Columbia, and Washington, DC.

Today Re-form operates a 50,000-square-foot warehouse and production facility in Baltimore where nearly 50 skilled upholsterers, painters, woodworkers, warehouse technicians, installers, designers, and project managers handle warehousing, inventory management, furniture delivery and installation, office decommissioning, space planning, and furniture refurbishment. The facility supports remanufacturing of Herman Miller, Haworth, and Steelcase systems furniture, along with paint refinishing, seating reupholstery, and laminate fabrication. An online inventory portal gives clients remote access to stored assets and allows them to request delivery or installation.

The company serves enterprise-sized corporations, government agencies, and other organizations undergoing relocation, renovation, consolidation, or new-space openings throughout the Mid-Atlantic. It also taps a national installation network for out-of-state projects. Clients rely on Re-form for coordinated workplace transitions that encompass asset tracking, responsible reuse and recycling, and phased deployment.

Re-form positions itself as a single-source partner for workplace logistics, emphasizing practical, flexible solutions that reduce waste, control costs, and extend the useful life of existing furniture. Its combined services—warehousing, asset management, installation, decommissioning, and design—are intended to keep organizations organized and adaptable as workplace needs change.

old_description: ReNu has been working with insurance providers since 2012 and is able to help you navigate your insurance claim from hail or wind.  Our experts will guide you through the insurance process and make things easy for you.  Hail damage can be hard to spot and small crack from hail could result in pathways for water to enter your home and comprise the function of your roof.   We are experts in finding hail damage and working with insurance carriers to approve claims for hail-damaged roofs.  If a hail or wind storm has hit your area contact the experts at ReNu today!
about:
ReNu Solar & Roofing operates from Harrisburg, Pennsylvania, serving residential customers across central and eastern Pennsylvania and into Maryland. The company traces its roots to roofing, with its founders leveraging that expertise to expand into solar installation and energy storage. It has worked with insurance providers on hail and wind damage claims since 2012.

The firm provides turnkey solar, roofing, and battery storage installation for homeowners. Its process covers free in-home consultation, custom system design using CAD software, permitting, utility coordination, installation, and final inspection. ReNu handles all steps in-house, avoiding subcontractors, and partners with SolarEdge and Enphase for storage equipment. The company offers 25-year warranties on workmanship, full system performance, and energy production.

ReNu serves residential property owners in counties including Mifflin, Juniata, Snyder, Berks, and the areas around Philadelphia and Baltimore. Its customers are typically homeowners seeking to reduce electricity bills, sell excess power to utilities, and protect against rising energy rates. The company also assists with insurance claims for storm-damaged roofs.

ReNu differentiates itself through undivided responsibility—clients have a single point of contact for both roofing and solar work—and through its 25-year transferable warranties that include a watertight roof penetration guarantee. The firm emphasizes local, experienced staff and a streamlined, no-subcontractor model.

name: Reclaiming Iowa
old_description: Reclaiming Iowa specializes in custom commercial and residential heirloom furniture and decor made from locally sourced reclaimed timbers and hardwoods.
about:
Reclaiming Iowa operates from West Des Moines, Iowa, where it was founded in 2008 by Kevin Dubay. Dubay holds a Bachelor of Fine Arts from the Kansas City Art Institute and a Master's in Furniture Design and Manufacturing from the University of Arizona, and he launched the studio to combine artistic vision with hands-on craftsmanship.

The company builds custom commercial and residential heirloom furniture and architectural woodwork using locally sourced reclaimed timbers and live‑edge hardwood slabs. Every piece is made to order — about 90 percent of projects are fully custom — and the workshop handles everything from consultation and design through handcrafting, kiln‑drying slabs to 6 percent moisture content, and finishing with a durable hard wax oil. Restoration services are not offered.

Clients span residential homeowners and a range of commercial sectors: restaurants and bars (dining tables, bar tops, back bars, feature walls), retail (countertops, shelving, product displays), and office or flex spaces (conference tables, desks, reception pieces). The studio has completed projects for businesses across Iowa, delivering and installing each piece statewide at no extra charge.

Dubay started Reclaiming Iowa to provide furniture that fits a client's exact space and style while preserving the history of salvaged wood. When possible, pieces are labeled with the original building name, location, and construction date, turning each item into a conversation piece and an environmentally sustainable choice.
